# flatc release-asset checksums, one row per version, keyed by the version
# `action.yml` beside this file derives from the workspace manifest's exact
# `flatbuffers` requirement.
#
# These are checksums of the one release asset CI fetches. **The asset name is
# not written here** — it lives once, in `action.yml`'s `asset=` line, because
# it changes on its own schedule: it encodes the libstdc++ the binary was built
# against, so a future `g++-14` build renames it. The derive command below reads
# it from there rather than repeating it, so a rename cannot leave this file
# hashing an asset CI does not fetch.
#
# A version with no row fails the install rather than fetching bytes nothing
# checks, so bumping `flatbuffers` in Cargo.toml means adding a row in the same
# commit. That is the point: the failure is loud and names the missing version,
# where a hardcoded sum would have gone stale silently.
#
# Derive a row, reading both the version and the asset the way the action does.
# The last line prints the row itself, in this file's column order — do not
# paste `sha256sum` output directly, which is the other order and would key the
# row on the checksum:
#
#   v=$(awk -F'"' '/^flatbuffers = "=/{print $2}' Cargo.toml | tr -d '=')
#   a=$(awk -F"'" '/^ *asset=/{print $2}' \
#         .github/actions/install-flatc/action.yml)
#   gh release download "v${v}" --repo google/flatbuffers --pattern "${a}" \
#     --clobber
#   printf '%s    %s\n' "${v}" "$(sha256sum "${a}" | awk '{print $1}')"
#
# The `tr` is load-bearing: the awk half alone yields `=25.12.19`, which matches
# no row and fails closed on every run.
#
# Rows are `version<space>sha256`. Comment lines cannot collide with a version,
# so the lookup ignores them without a rule of its own.
#
# version   sha256
25.12.19    9f87066dc5dfa7fe02090b55bab5f3e55df03e32c9b0cdf229004ade7d091039
